payload.title: Wedding Place Cards Ideas for Every Table
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: A couple in their 30s, about a year out from a destination or luxury wedding of 60 to 120 guests, who has a seating plan forming and is now shopping for a place card idea that suits the setting, survives the venue (wind, heat, travel) and can be sourced or made without stress.
payload.primary_persona: planner_couple (Sophie & James); secondary search_visitor (Priya) for the shopping intent
payload.goal: Browse stationers on Wedded Marketplace to find someone to make the chosen place cards (one action). Secondary: Wonderland Studio for the seating plan in the practical section; Wedded Advisor line at the close.
payload.angle: Lead with ideas, grouped by style so a couple can shortlist in a minute, then answer what idea lists skip: how a place card works with the seating plan, and what changes when the cards have to travel or be made in another country (print at home and carry, or print near the venue). Written for a guest list where names, titles and spelling matter as much as the look.
must_include: Opening that leads straight into ideas (shopping intent); keep the intro to two or three short paragraphs.
Place cards versus escort cards: one paragraph, placed early, linking /wedding-tools/escort-cards-vs-place-cards.

Ideas grouped by style, de-duplicated from both old posts and fully rewritten in our own words. Groups: (1) classic stationery (calligraphy or hand-lettered cards, tiles, marble or stone-look cards, bookmarks); (2) natural and edible (leaves, rosemary rings or herb sprigs, fruit such as a lemon, macarons or biscuits, sweets); (3) keepsakes and favours (personalised glassware or shot glasses, small stones or agate, slate hearts, keys, a small plant); (4) glass, mirror and acrylic (acrylic laser-cut names, mirror cards, names on wine glasses); (5) destination and local (shells for a beach setting, wine cork holders for a vineyard, a local fruit or material from the region); (6) on the napkin or plate (a name tag tied to the napkin, a card resting on the plate or a menu with the name printed). Recommended count: about 20 ideas in total, 3 to 4 per group, each with one or two sentences on when it suits and one practical note.

Practical details: check spelling and titles (Dr, Mr and Mrs, preferred names) against one source; the seating plan as the single source of names, with Wonderland Studio (/wonderland-studio) as our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs; legibility (size, contrast, low evening light); allergens and labelling if edible; outdoor wind (weight, holders, attaching to napkins or glassware); printing lead time as advice only, no figures (order after RSVPs close and leave room for late changes and a proof).

Destination weddings, written as questions the couple works through: print locally near the venue or make at home and carry? Will the cards survive luggage, humidity and heat? Who sets them out on the day? Can local produce or materials stand in for imported ones?
Finding a stationer: one short section pointing to Wedded Marketplace (/marketplace) to browse stationers and vendors. No vendor names or vendor pages.
FAQ (4 to 6 questions), e.g. do you need place cards if you have escort cards; what goes on a place card; who gets a place card; when to order or make them; can place cards double as favours.

Close with one Wedded Advisor line drawn only from brand-facts.md lines 19 to 30 (for example: one Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, as a single point of contact) linking /wonderland-concierge with UTM.
avoid: Any prices, costs or statistics (no figures at all, including lead-time numbers).
'Best', 'unique', 'must-have', 'stunning' or other overclaims; the old titles' 'unique' and 'unconventional' framing.
Research talk ('our research shows', 'we analysed', 'top results').
Vendor, maker, Etsy shop, photographer, Instagram handle or publication names, credits or links; no /vendor/ or /venue/ pages.
Reusing any image from either old post (all are third-party Instagram, Etsy or blog images, unlicensed).
Competitor branding or wording (Easy Weddings or any other).
Non-wedding uses from the 17 post (birthday, christening, Thanksgiving, kitchen tea, baby shower, kids' candy necklaces).
Puns as headings carried over from the 25 post ('Marble At This', 'Shell You Be Unique', 'Leaf' etc.).
Unsupported claims such as 'guests will keep this forever', 'luxurious and expensive touch', 'no one keeps paper place cards'.
Em dashes; US spelling (use Australian English).
payload.cannibalisation_check: Merge, not a new page. Kept URL /25-unique-place-cards-for-your-wedding absorbs /17-unconventional-yet-stunning-place-cards (same intent, place card ideas; 301 the 17 post to the kept URL at publish). Related but distinct: /wedding-tools/escort-cards-vs-place-cards owns the difference between the two (we link it, one paragraph only); /expert-advice/wedding-seating-chart and /expert-advice/how-to-make-a-wedding-seating-chart own the seating chart how-to; /expert-advice/where-to-print-wedding-seating-chart owns printing and sizes; /expert-advice/our-favourite-interactive-seating-charts owns seating chart displays. This post owns wedding place card ideas. No other link-map row targets 'wedding place cards'.
